subject: ent
title: Otosclerosis and conductive deafness

steps.tx: **Key point.** Conductive deafness arises when sound fails through canal, drum or ossicles: wax, perforation, effusion, ossicular erosion or fixation. Air conduction falls while bone conduction stays normal, creating an air bone gap on audiometry, with Rinne negative and Weber lateralising to the worse ear on tuning fork tests. The pattern, not just severity, directs the search.
steps.say: Blocked sound path deafens air conduction while bone stays normal. Tuning forks point to the bad ear in conductive loss.

steps.tx: **Otosclerosis** is abnormal bone remodelling of the otic capsule fixing the stapes footplate, causing slowly progressive conductive loss in young adults, often women, worsening in pregnancy, with family history and normal drums. Tinnitus accompanies, and speech discrimination stays good. Bilateral disease is usual over time.
steps.say: Otosclerosis glues the stapes in young adults, often women, slowly deafening with normal drums and family pattern.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Audiometry shows air bone gap with a characteristic dip in bone conduction at 2000 Hz (Carhart notch), an artefact of stapes fixation rather than cochlear damage. Tympanometry stiffens (As type) and stapedial reflex vanishes. Schwartze sign, a pink blush behind the drum from vascular active bone, appears in a minority. CT can show lucency at the fissula ante fenestram in active disease.
steps.say: Carhart notch at 2 kHz with stiff drum tracing marks stapes fixation. Pink blush behind drum is the uncommon Schwartze sign.

vis.alt: An audiogram illustrating conductive hearing loss due to otosclerosis, featuring a prominent air-bone gap and a specific dip in bone conduction at 2000 Hz, known as the Carhart notch.
vis.caption: Audiogram showing conductive loss with characteristic Carhart notch in otosclerosis. Image: Perkins CJ, Mitchell S. Audiology Clinical Masking. [Updated 2022 Mar , CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Management offers amplification or **stapes surgery** (stapedotomy with piston prosthesis) restoring the gap in most operated ears, with small risks of sensorineural loss, vertigo and taste change via chorda tympani. Sodium fluoride historically aimed to slow active cochlear disease but is not standard cure. Cochlear otosclerosis adds sensorineural loss needing aids or implants when severe.
steps.say: Hearing aids or stapes piston surgery close the gap. Surgery risks inner ear, so counselling matters.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Other fixation and discontinuity causes matter: tympanosclerosis plaques after chronic infection stiffen drum and ossicles, traumatic incus dislocation interrupts the chain after head injury (often with haemotympanum), and congenital fixation presents from childhood without progression pattern of otosclerosis. Surgical exploration with ossiculoplasty addresses selected mechanical defects.
steps.say: Scarred stiff drums, dislocated incus after trauma and congenital fixation mimic otosclerosis. History separates them.
